title: Sparse Attention Patterns via Dynamic Top-K Routing in Edge Devices
abstract: Large language models often exhibit heavy quadratic latency during long-context processing. We introduce Dynamic Top-K Routing (DTR), a sub-quadratic attention approximation that computes sparse key-value activations adaptively based on query entropy. Evaluated across LLaMA-3 architectures, DTR reduces inference latency by 41% with negligible degradation on standard reasoning benchmarks (GSM8k, HumanEval).

title: Latent Diffusion for 3D Molecular Conformation Sampling in Drug Discovery
abstract: Generating thermodynamically stable 3D molecular conformations is crucial for computational drug design. We propose Mol-LatentDiff, an SE(3)-equivariant latent diffusion model that operates directly within learned low-dimensional torsion-angle manifolds rather than raw Euclidean coordinates, demonstrating 3.2x faster convergence and superior validity on QM9 and GEOM-Drugs.

title: Mitigating Sycophancy in Multi-Turn Reasoning via Preference Graph Alignment
abstract: RLHF fine-tuned LLMs frequently conform to incorrect user priors during extended dialogues. We formalize this sycophancy phenomenon as a bias in the trajectory reward surface and propose Preference Graph Alignment (PGA). Across 1,500 debate prompts, PGA reduces false concessions by 68% while retaining polite demeanor and factual accuracy.

title: Zero-Shot Video Grounding with Hierarchical Temporal Flow Transformers
abstract: We present FlowFormer-Z, a hierarchical vision-language model for spatiotemporal localization of arbitrary natural language queries in untrimmed video streams without downstream fine-tuning. By coupling optical flow tokens with self-supervised cross-attention heads, we achieve a new state-of-the-art on Charades-STA and ActivityNet Captions.

title: Information-Theoretic Generalization Bounds for Overparameterized Deep Ensembles
abstract: While deep ensembles consistently outperform single models in calibration and error rates, theoretical guarantees remain fragmented. We derive PAC-Bayesian excess risk bounds parameterized by mutual information between ensemble components and data manifold curvature.

title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning on Brain EEG Signals for Motor Imagery Decoding
abstract: Neural decoding of raw electroencephalography (EEG) suffers from severe cross-subject variability. We present WaveMAE, a masked autoencoder trained on 10,000+ hours of multi-channel physiological recordings, setting a new benchmark for non-invasive brain-computer interfaces.
